doc.title: Dick Griffin interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, February 12, 2024

title: Improvising horn parts, Roy Haynes, and Sullivan's reaction
summary: Griffin describes making up parts like a doo wop group player, the excited mood offstage, and Sullivan's stunned reaction.

blocks.x: Yeah. And that’s one thing I did. See being with Rahsaan, a lot of the stuff he played was — I just played it because of my doo wop experience of playing with the full group, like “Say a Little Prayer” the first time everything came out just right because I was thinking like a doo wop group player [scats] that was made up right on the spot. [scats] And I would make up all those arrangements right on the spot out of my head [scats]. I could hear my part just like if I was singing in a vocal group and it was made up and nothing was personable and it was just like that’s it you know. And the background was the same thing. That was made up right on the spot. We had never played that background, I just heard, you know, [scats] and McGhee, Charles McGhee — we were so tight because we had been playing with Rahsaan and he knew, he had perfect pitch as well and he could really match me real — so all of that was as crisp as you can get it, right on the spot.
Well when you all walked off the stage, can you remember the conversation?

Yes. Okay? Everybody was — like excited, oh wow. Roy Haynes, see that was my time to play with Roy Haynes you know. Roy Haynes to the day, it’s like a really — everything he plays is different and innovative and fresh you know. And he mentioned somebody asked him about rudiments and everything and he said, “I don’t do that because these hands are uneven” or something. He mentioned something like that. But oh, it was just — everybody was like wow — magic happened, and nothing was really rehearsed ‘cause we thought we were going to be playing “My Cherie Amour” [scats]. And it was going to be just real kind of a soothing, organized performance, but it was wow. And everybody got to hear it.
And Ed’s comment afterwards, I forget his exact words but it just put a whole, I don’t know it was quite humorous.
Yeah. He was — he didn’t know what to say he was just like whoa.
And then where did that come from? And then we went into the Dixie — we called it the New Orleans style music, oh that was just it.
Yeah. I was thinking how is he going to get out of this? How is Rahsaan going to wrap this up in short, he did.
Yeah. That was the magic of him.
